runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mixed on Thursday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 declining 0.71% to close near 60,816 as Nvidia-linked suppliers fell sharply following overnight reports that the chip giant's board was weighing a leadership change. USD/JPY pushed to approximately 159.8, effectively unwinding prior Bank of Japan intervention levels, as October US CPI came in hotter than forecast at +0.4% m/m headline and +0.3% core — cementing expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate hike. Tech-heavy indices in Seoul and Taiwan also declined while Australia's ASX held modestly positive on materials support.

European markets opened broadly higher, bucking the tech-led US pre-market weakness. The DAX surged 1.20% to 26,662 on strong manufacturing orders and relief that the EU and UK may delay a 10% tariff on electric vehicles; the FTSE 100 added 0.78% to 10,835 after UK growth data showed tentative stabilization. Energy names provided support as oil steadied following a brief dip on easing Iran-related geopolitical fears, while European bank stocks gained on the prospect of a higher-for-longer rate environment after the hot US CPI print.

US pre-market is under pressure heading into Thursday's open, led by a 5-6% drop in Nvidia after reports its board is considering replacing CEO Jensen Huang — a headline that rattled confidence in the AI trade broadly. S&P 500 futures are down approximately 0.43% near 7,586, while Nasdaq-100 futures are off roughly 0.9%. The Dow is fractionally positive at ~52,522, insulated by its lower tech weighting. Multiple firms — Bernstein, Baird, and Evercore — downgraded Nvidia overnight, with targets ranging from $186 to $200. Counterintuitively, storage names (Seagate +8.65%) and AMD (+upgraded to Outperform at William Blair) are catching a bid on rotation out of Nvidia into alternative AI-infrastructure plays. The overarching macro story remains the hot October CPI: a December Fed hike is now viewed as near-certain, pushing the dollar to a 19-month high and weighing on rate-sensitive equities.

ideas.catalyst: Reports that NVIDIA's board is weighing replacing CEO Jensen Huang sparked a 5-6% pre-market selloff and triggered downgrades from Bernstein (Market Perform, $200), Baird (Neutral, $200), and Evercore (In-Line, $186).
ideas.thesis: Executive uncertainty at NVIDIA removes the primary narrative pillar that has sustained the stock's premium multiple; with earnings due November 17, any miss or cautious guidance could compound the leadership-risk discount. Even a resolution of the CEO question may not fully restore confidence ahead of the report, keeping the stock under pressure in the near term.
ideas.key_risk: Positive resolution of the leadership question before Nov 17, or a strong earnings/guidance beat, could trigger a violent short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: CoreWeave reported strong Q3 revenue, beat estimates, and raised its full-year outlook on November 11, sending shares up 20.74% — the standout gainer of the prior session.
ideas.thesis: As the leading independent GPU cloud provider, CoreWeave is a primary beneficiary of AI compute demand that is structurally decoupled from NVIDIA's internal corporate drama; hyperscaler customers cannot easily substitute away from its infrastructure capacity. The earnings beat and raised guidance validate that neocloud adoption continues to accelerate even as AI hardware names face uncertainty.
ideas.key_risk: Any NVIDIA CEO resolution that reignites enthusiasm for direct NVDA longs could cause rotation out of proxies like CRWV.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance – Stock Market News Nov 12

ideas.catalyst: Coherent surged 18% on November 11 as AI-driven demand for high-speed optical transceivers and networking equipment continued to outpace supply; the move followed CoreWeave's earnings beat highlighting capacity investment.
ideas.thesis: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure build-outs require massive upgrades to intra-data-center and backbone optical networking, and Coherent is one of the few companies with scale across transceivers, components, and compound semiconductor materials. The 18% single-day move likely has follow-through as institutional investors rotate into optical infrastructure as a picks-and-shovels AI play insulated from the NVDA leadership overhang.
ideas.key_risk: A broader tech risk-off if the NVDA CEO situation escalates could drag COHR lower despite its structural story.

ideas.theme: AI Chip Rotation / NVDA Share Capture
ideas.catalyst: William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform on November 12, while AMD gained ~9.79% in a recent session; Nvidia's leadership crisis creates an opening for AMD's MI300/MI400 AI accelerators to gain enterprise consideration.
ideas.thesis: Enterprise and cloud customers who have been heavily concentrated in NVIDIA GPUs may begin dual-sourcing or accelerating AMD roadmap evaluations given the leadership uncertainty risk — particularly for new datacenter commitments. AMD is trading at a significant discount to NVDA on a forward P/E basis while its AI GPU roadmap is competitive for most inference workloads.
ideas.key_risk: If NVDA's CEO situation resolves quickly and the Nov 17 earnings beat, AMD's relative-value thesis loses its near-term catalyst.

ideas.catalyst: October CPI printed hotter than expected (+0.4% m/m headline, +0.3% core), cementing expectations for a December Fed rate hike and pushing the 10-year yield toward 4.67% as of this morning.
ideas.thesis: With headline and core CPI both beating estimates and Fed officials (including Goolsbee) flagging concern about the data, the bond market is repricing for a higher-for-longer trajectory; the 10-year yield has further to run as the December hike gets priced in and the market begins discounting 2027 cuts being pushed out. TBT provides leveraged inverse exposure to long-duration Treasuries and benefits from rising yields.
ideas.key_risk: A sudden deterioration in US economic data or a risk-off credit event could drive a flight-to-safety rally in Treasuries, compressing yields and hurting TBT.

ideas.theme: China AI Chip Self-Sufficiency / Spinoff Value Unlock
ideas.catalyst: Alibaba's T-Head AI chip unit received HKEX approval to file for a Hong Kong IPO (announced Nov 10-12), and DZ Bank upgraded BABA to Buy with a $140 target, arguing the spinoff unlocks embedded chip unit value.
ideas.thesis: The T-Head IPO will crystallize value in Alibaba's AI chip capabilities at a time when China's tech sector is prioritizing domestic semiconductor alternatives to NVIDIA; a successful listing could unlock 5-10% of BABA's current market cap in standalone chip unit value. The DZ Bank upgrade reflects growing recognition that Alibaba's cloud and AI assets are undervalued relative to US cloud peers, with the HK listing serving as a re-rating catalyst.
ideas.key_risk: Regulatory risk from Chinese authorities or HKEX listing committee rejecting the structure; US-China trade tensions escalating could pressure all Chinese ADRs.

sources.label: Benzinga – Alibaba T-Head Hong Kong IPO

ideas.catalyst: Seagate shares are up 8.65% in pre-market trading on November 12, driven by its positioning as a beneficiary of AI-driven data storage demand that is decoupled from NVIDIA's internal drama.
ideas.thesis: Every AI training and inference workload generates massive amounts of data that must be stored; Seagate's high-capacity HDD business is seeing accelerating demand from hyperscalers building out AI infrastructure, and the stock had lagged optical and GPU names despite the same secular tailwind. The pre-market move suggests institutional buyers are rotating into storage as a defensive AI infrastructure exposure.
ideas.key_risk: If the AI infrastructure buildout pauses or hyperscaler capex guidance disappoints, Seagate would be directly impacted as one of the primary picks-and-shovels beneficiaries.

ideas.company: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund
ideas.catalyst: The US dollar reached a 19-month high after October CPI beat estimates, pushing USD/JPY to approximately 159.8 as the probability of a December Fed rate hike rose sharply; the dollar is diverging from other G10 central banks that remain on hold or cutting.
ideas.thesis: With US inflation re-accelerating and the Fed forced toward another hike while ECB, BOE, and BOJ remain cautious, rate differentials are moving decisively in favor of the USD; this dynamic typically sustains multi-week dollar uptrends and UUP provides clean, liquid USD index exposure. A December hike confirmation from Fed minutes or Fedspeak in coming weeks would reinforce the trade.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise dovish Fed pivot or sharp US growth miss could reverse dollar strength quickly; intervention by BOJ near 160 is an additional wildcard.

ideas.catalyst: Barrick Mining filed for the NYSE IPO of its North American business as 'American Barrick Gold' (ABGC), with Goldman Sachs, BofA, and RBC as underwriters, and a $1.2B annual dividend structure built into the spinoff.
ideas.thesis: The spinoff crystallizes valuation for Barrick's North American assets at a moment when gold remains elevated near $2,638/oz and the North American operations have among the lowest all-in sustaining costs in the industry; the guaranteed $1.2B annual dividend from the new entity to Barrick also creates a value-of-parts argument for holding the parent at current prices. IPO-driven re-rating events in mining typically expand the NAV multiple for the parent.
ideas.key_risk: Gold price decline driven by a stronger dollar or risk-on rotation would compress NAV across all gold miners; IPO timing risk if markets deteriorate.

ideas.catalyst: Capricor's cell therapy Deramiocel for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy has an FDA action date around November 22, and labeling hint analysis by investors is reportedly skewing positive; shares have been rallying ahead of the decision.
ideas.thesis: Deramiocel would be the first cell therapy approved for DMD, a rare and fatal disease with significant unmet need and substantial orphan drug pricing power; FDA advisory committee signals and labeling hints that investors are scrutinizing appear favorable. A clean approval could send CAPR shares up 100-200% given its small market cap relative to the commercial opportunity.
ideas.key_risk: This is a high-conviction binary trade: a Complete Response Letter or approval with heavy restrictions/REMS requirements would be severely negative for the stock; position sizing must reflect the binary risk.

deals.headline: Alibaba Receives HKEX Clearance to File T-Head AI Chip Unit IPO
deals.description: Alibaba's in-house AI chip design unit T-Head has received approval from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to proceed with an IPO filing, subject to listing committee review and China Securities Regulatory Commission clearance. The listing will keep T-Head as an Alibaba subsidiary while creating a separate public market valuation for China's most advanced domestically designed AI accelerators.
deals.impact: High – Unlocks embedded chip unit value; positions China's AI semiconductor sector as a credible NVIDIA competitor narrative for investors

deals.headline: Barrick Mining Files NYSE IPO for North American Spinoff 'American Barrick Gold' (ABGC)
deals.description: Barrick Mining Corp. has filed with the SEC to spin off and separately list its North American gold mining assets on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker ABGC, with Goldman Sachs, Bank of America Securities, and RBC Capital Markets as joint bookrunners. The post-split structure includes a fixed $1.2 billion annual dividend payable quarterly from the new entity to Barrick, providing an income floor for the parent's shareholders.
deals.impact: Medium-High – Valuation unlock for a tier-1 gold mining asset at current elevated gold prices

deals.headline: Aon North America Advances $17B Acquisition of USI Advantage Corp.
deals.description: Aon North America's proposed $17 billion acquisition of USI Advantage Corp., one of the largest insurance brokerage transactions of 2026, continues to advance through regulatory review as the combined entity would create the world's second-largest commercial insurance broker. The deal, announced earlier in Q3 2026, is under review by the DOJ Antitrust Division with a decision expected before year-end.
deals.impact: High – Creates dominant commercial insurance broker; regulatory outcome is a binary catalyst for AON shares
deals.source: S&P Global Market Intelligence via ANI

deals.headline: argenx Agrees to Acquire Unnatural Products to Expand Antibody Platform
deals.description: argenx SE has entered into an agreement to acquire biotech startup Unnatural Products, which has developed proprietary technology for engineering antibodies with non-natural amino acids to improve potency and half-life. The deal expands argenx's pipeline beyond its core efgartigimod franchise and strengthens its platform capabilities ahead of multiple late-stage readouts in 2027.
deals.impact: Medium – Strategic platform expansion; bolt-on deal consistent with argenx's track record of platform-building M&A

deals.headline: Marks & Spencer Partners with Global Fashion Group for Asia Pacific Expansion
deals.description: Marks & Spencer has entered a strategic partnership with Global Fashion Group (GFG) to sell its clothing and home products through GFG's platforms in Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, with logistics and fulfillment handled by GFG's existing regional network. The deal is expected to launch on The Iconic in Australia and New Zealand in early 2027, marking M&S's first significant Asia Pacific e-commerce presence.
deals.impact: Low-Medium – Opens new markets for M&S; meaningful for GFG as a large-brand endorsement of its platform
